These toxins, which are left undetected in humans in their 30s and 40s, appear as chronic diseases in their 50s and 60s. Especially, cancer, which many people are afraid of, is caused by mutations in the body for five to 10 years because it doesn't release these toxins.

In order to do that, you have to eat the basic vegetables and fruits.
In order for us humans to get energy, there are basically three essential nutrients: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and in order for these nutrients to be digested and absorbed by the body and converted into energy, we need a substance called enzymes.

It's a small protein structure called Enzyme, for example, amylase, lipase, and trypsin, which we often hear in school, are digestive enzymes. It is a really important enzyme that functions to digest and absorb starch, fat, and protein that makes up food, and plays an important role in smooth metabolism and health maintenance.

Enzymes are basically produced in the body, but if enzymes are used a lot due to wrong habits, lifestyle habits, adult diseases such as obesity, lack of exercise, and excessive stress such as smoking, the lack of enzymes can occur in the body. In this case, we can make up for the enzymes that we lack by eating fresh food.

Enzymes are made up of proteins and react sensitively to external environments such as temperature and pH, so they lose their function unless they are under appropriate conditions. The cooking process of applying heat, such as boiling or steaming, destroys enzymes, and if you eat these heated and cooked foods, your body lacks enzymes. Food that has been heat-treated and enzymes destroyed also slows digestion, so it is easy to decay in the process, which can produce intestinal toxins, which can increase the incidence of colon cancer.

Studies have shown that cooking or eating only canned food, in accordance with the Standard American Diet (SAD), where fruits and vegetables are not sufficiently supplied, increases chronic degenerative diseases and early death rates.

A U.S. study found that rats were fed heated and cooked food at an 80% rate for 135 days, and the weight of the pancreas increased by 20-30%. This means that if you eat mainly cooked food, the pancreas was stimulated to work more. Our bodies can produce enzymes on their own, but we need more enzymes than usual, and we need to get them supplied with live enzymes through unheated raw food intake.

Enzymes cannot artificially increase their quantity, and only raw vegetables contain this "functioning living enzyme." Fiber, which sweeps down barriers and cleans them cleanly, is important in modern people's diet, but enzymes that help digestion and absorb important nutrients are more important.

It is time to pay attention to the intake of food enzymes that promote metabolism, prevent various diseases, and help maintain health. The germ of the seed, the germ of the grain, is very rich in enzymes. In addition, enzymes are contained in various foods such as kiwis, pineapples, ginger, and soybean paste fermented by breaking down proteins.

Typically, when you eat fresh fruits or vegetables, you often eat them with the idea of eating fiber, but fiber is not always good. There are nutrients necessary for the body between the fibers, but it is also difficult to consume nutrients efficiently because they are not easily decomposed in the body. In this case, if you grind and drink green juice, it can be a fresh nutritional supplement rich in live enzymes, various vitamins, and minerals, which can be a way to revitalize the body in a short time.

Let's add fresh fruits or vegetables to each meal to supplement the enzymes that our bodies are likely to lack with food.

In our teenage years, our natural immunity and ability to detoxify helped us overcome toxins smoothly. As we entered our 20s, many of us began drinking alcohol and smoking, but we didn't experience many health problems due to the short period of accumulation. However, as we enter our 30s, we may start to feel the changes in our body caused by these toxins. Unfortunately, toxins that go undetected in our 30s and 40s can lead to chronic diseases in our 50s and 60s, including cancer, caused by mutations that occur over a period of five to ten years when toxins are not released.

Therefore, it's crucial for people in their 50s and 60s to pay attention to their bodies, which may have been neglected due to their busy schedules in their earlier years. One way to do this is by consuming basic vegetables and fruits, which provide the essential nutrients needed to produce energy. These nutrients, such as carbohydrates, proteins, and fats, need to be digested and absorbed by the body to be converted into energy, a process that requires enzymes.

Enzymes, such as amylase, lipase, and trypsin, are essential for smooth metabolism and health maintenance. While our bodies naturally produce enzymes, wrong habits and lifestyle habits, such as obesity, lack of exercise, excessive stress, and smoking, can cause a lack of enzymes. Fresh food can help replenish the enzymes we lack.

However, enzymes are sensitive to external environments, such as temperature and pH, and lose their function if they're not under appropriate conditions. Applying heat through cooking processes like boiling or steaming destroys enzymes, making it essential to consume unheated raw food to get live enzymes. Eating heat-treated and enzyme-destroyed food slows digestion, leading to intestinal toxins and an increased incidence of colon cancer.

Research shows that consuming only canned and cooked food, as in the Standard American Diet, which doesn't provide enough fruits and vegetables, increases the risk of chronic degenerative diseases and early death. In a study, rats fed 80% heated and cooked food for 135 days had a 20-30% increase in the weight of their pancreas, indicating that consuming mostly cooked food stimulates the pancreas to work harder. While our bodies can produce enzymes, we need to supplement them through unheated raw food intake to maintain good health.

Raw vegetables, including the germ of the seed and the germ of the grain, are rich in enzymes. Other foods, such as kiwis, pineapples, ginger, and soybean paste, fermented by breaking down proteins, also contain enzymes. While we often eat fresh fruits and vegetables for their fiber content, which is important in modern diets, we should also consider consuming nutrients efficiently by consuming live enzymes. Drinking green juice made by grinding and blending fresh fruits and vegetables can be a quick way to revitalize the body with live enzymes, vitamins, and minerals.

In conclusion, adding fresh fruits and vegetables to each meal can supplement the enzymes we may lack due to our diets and help promote metabolism, prevent various diseases, and maintain good health.
